target_customer: SMBs and business teams that keep data in spreadsheets, Airtable or databases and need portals and internal tools
problem: Teams need apps and customer portals on top of spreadsheet data without engineers.

founders.name: Michael Skelly
prior_employers: an asset management company (unnamed; built internal Salesforce apps)

technical_complexity.rationale: Connectors to spreadsheets and databases with a configurable UI layer; standard SaaS engineering with permissions and sync as the harder parts.

defensibility.rationale: Apps built on customer data create some lock-in, but the product is a layer over Airtable and similar tools that can add interfaces themselves.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources; the company was still operating in 2025-26 and launched Stacker AI and acquired Nocode.tech.

market_need_then: About 250 customers in Aug 2020 rising to 500 and $1M ARR by Jan 2021 per TechCrunch, mostly SMBs.

branding.domain_note: Uses stackerhq.com rather than an exact stacker.com domain.

brand_strength.rationale: Simple descriptive-feeling word, no mascot or brand press found; a common word shared by unrelated firms.

pivots.from: A more complex product that required heavy hand-holding
pivots.to: A simpler self-serve design (first version of the current product launched end of 2019)
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch Aug 2021, the founders moved to a simpler design.

outcome_analysis: Stacker simplified its product in 2019, reached about 500 customers and $1M ARR by January 2021 on a $1.7M seed, then raised a $20M Series A led by a16z in August 2021. It remains Active with a small team; no later round or exit is found, so this is a solid early success that stalled or went quiet after the 2021 round, with public data ending there.
notes: Batch: directory and YC page say Summer 2020; one source mentioned W20 (unverified). Total raised $23M per Crunchbase as cited by TechCrunch, which exceeds the two rounds ($21.7M), so a gap remains and coverage is partial. A UK outlet headlined $15M for the Series A (conflicts; $20M used). The TechCrunch articles name no dated competitors besides Airtable as the underlying tool, so the list is empty. Team size 4 on YC page conflicts with 19 employees in Aug 2021. Web Archive unreachable.
